name: LM4128AMF-1.8_NOPB
title: SOT-23 precision micropower series voltage reference
summary: The LM4128 is a series voltage reference in a 5-pin SOT-23, offered at 1.8 V, 2.048 V, 2.5 V, 3.0 V, 3.3 V and 4.096 V in four accuracy grades from 0.1% to 1.0%. It draws 60 µA typical, sources up to 20 mA with 400 mV max dropout at 10 mA, and an enable pin drops it to 3 µA. It needs only an input capacitor and stays stable with up to 10 µF on the output. Q1 versions are AEC-Q100 Grade 1.
key_figures: 75 ppm/°C max (A, B); 100 ppm/°C max (C, D)

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable; high turns the reference on, low shuts it down. Internal pull-up of about 2 µA; must not exceed VIN.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: Past these ratings the device may be damaged; the operating ratings are where it works, without the guaranteed limits of the electrical tables.

The 350 mW figure is with no added PCB copper. At higher ambient temperature the allowed dissipation falls as PDissMAX = (TJMAX - TA) / θJ-A, never above 350 mW; θJ-A is 220°C/W for SOT-23 and TJMAX is 125°C.
Human body model: 100 pF discharged into each pin through 1.5 kΩ.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The basic hookup: supply into VIN with a ceramic capacitor to ground, the reference taken from VREF, and EN brought out as a control input. CIN must be fitted; COUT may be left off.

parts.note: required; ceramic X5R or X7R, CIN ≥ COUT, at least 0.1 µF with no COUT

circuits.title: Voltage reference with complementary output
circuits.description: An op amp on ±5 V inverts the reference to give a negative output of equal size: two equal resistors R set a gain of -1 from VREF, and R/2 goes from the non-inverting input to ground. Both +VREF and -VREF are brought out.

circuits.title: Precision voltage reference with force and sense output
circuits.description: A buffer op amp on +5 V takes VREF at its non-inverting input and drives the VREF_FORCE line; the VREF_SENSE line returns to its inverting input. A 0.1 µF capacitor and a 100 kΩ resistor sit from VREF to ground.

circuits.title: Programmable current source
circuits.description: The reference's GND pin sits on top of the 1 kΩ load RL, with R1 (500 Ω) and the adjustable RSET in series from VREF to that node. The load current is IOUT = VREF / (R1 + RSET) + IGND. A 0.1 µF capacitor joins VREF to the GND pin.

parts.note: adjustable; wiper joined to its R1 end

operation.text: Six fixed outputs are offered: 1.8 V, 2.048 V, 2.5 V, 3.0 V, 3.3 V and 4.096 V, coded -1.8, -2.0, -2.5, -3.0, -3.3 and -4.1 in the part number. Each comes in four grades by the letter after LM4128: A is ±0.1% initial and 75 ppm/°C, B ±0.2% and 75 ppm/°C, C ±0.5% and 100 ppm/°C, D ±1.0% and 100 ppm/°C. Parts with Q1 in the number are AEC-Q100 Grade 1 qualified and built on an automotive flow. MF parts ship 1000 per reel, MFX parts 3000. Other outputs from 1.8 V to 4.096 V can be made to order.

As a series reference it draws only its own 60 µA typical quiescent current when unloaded, rather than standing at full load current as a shunt reference would. Dropout is 400 mV max at 10 mA, and the part sources up to 20 mA.
The reference voltage is built from the gate-source voltages of on-chip transistors, working on the band-gap principle.

VIN must stay above VREF + 400 mV for loads up to 10 mA. EN has an internal pull-up current source of about 2 µA, so it may be left open or driven; when no external signal controls it, it may be tied to VIN. The part does not work properly with VEN above VIN. A low on EN is at most 35% of VIN and a high at least 65% of VIN. Pulling EN low cuts supply current to 3 µA typical.

A small X5R or X7R ceramic capacitor on VIN is required for stability, and its value must be at least COUT. With no output capacitor, CIN is 0.1 µF minimum. Larger CIN, typically 4.7 µF to 22 µF, can lower output noise and much reduce start-up overshoot; a further bypass capacitor from VIN to ground can lower noise more. With CIN fitted, the output drives any mix of resistance down to VREF/20 mA and capacitance up to 10 µF. No output capacitor is needed, and it is stable with up to 10 µF on the output. An output capacitor markedly improves the response to a light-to-heavy load step, but a very large one lengthens turn-on and slows line and load transients. Low-ESR ceramics are the usual choice, placed close to the part.
With VREF shorted to ground the output current is limited to 75 mA, and the short may last indefinitely.
Turn-on time, to 90% of the final output, depends on the load capacitance: typically 33.2 µs with 1 µF and 78.8 µs with 10 µF. Under brown-out at -40 °C it can stretch to as long as 10 ms.
Thermal hysteresis is the difference between the 25 °C output before and after a temperature swing. Across -40 °C to 125 °C it is 190 µV.

Drift is the spread between highest and lowest output over the operating range, divided by the nominal output and the range width. It is 75 ppm/°C max for A and B grades and 100 ppm/°C max for C and D grades, over -40 °C to 125 °C.
Typical drift is 50 ppm over 1000 hours, measured on 5 units of every voltage option at VIN = 5 V, unloaded, at room temperature.

SOT packages pick up less board-mounting stress than SOIC. Board flex can shift the initial output, so the part is best placed where the board bends least, near an edge or corner. A U-shaped slot cut around the footprint isolates it mechanically and also thermally. Bypass capacitors go close to the pins to keep trace parasitics small.
ESD protection on chip is limited: store and handle with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam so the MOS gates are not damaged.
